_comment: Crewflow image release-gate policy (H5). Read by image_gate.py; never shipped in an image. Every rule here is enforced fail-closed: 'block' items fail in every mode, 'release' items fail a release-mode run and are shown as NEEDS OWNER APPROVAL (HOLD) on pull requests. How to change this file: packages/rab-docker/docs/IMAGE_SECURITY_RELEASE_POLICY.md.

dockerfiles._comment: FROM references that are neither a digest-pinned image nor an earlier stage. Each needs a reason; the gate checks the result instead (worker-base: the Worker's lower layers must be exactly the gated API image's layers).

packages/rab-docker/rab/Dockerfile.worke.reason: Built FROM the API image of the same commit, which CI passes as an OCI-layout build context pinned by digest; the worker-base check proves the layer chain.

worker._exposed_ports: Inherited from the API base image (a Dockerfile cannot remove an inherited EXPOSE; it is metadata only and neither Worker child listens). Any other port fails.
worker._forbidden: P5 (PDF renderer migration): the Worker renders PDFs natively; Chromium, its driver and the OS packages only it pulled in must never return. forbidden_apk was derived from the MEASURED delta between the main 824f0824 Worker and API images (184 packages besides tini): it matches 149 of them (Chromium, ffmpeg and every codec, the X11/Wayland/Mesa/GTK stack, fonts, audio, libxml2, glib, cups-libs, cjson, ...); the 35 generic base libraries it does not name (libffi, pcre2, zstd-libs, xz-libs, sqlite-libs, libexpat, ...) are harmless alone and are not forbidden. fs FAILS (every mode) on any installed apk matching forbidden_apk or npm package matching forbidden_npm; attest FAILS if the SBOM names anything in sbom_must_not_include. Scoped to the runtime images only: the web e2e suite's own @playwright/test (rab-e2e-testing, CI runners) is untouched. Names ending in * are prefixes.

filesystem._comment: Code-loading paths: every non-symlink entry must be owned by 0:0 and not group/other-writable, except the listed runtime data directories (writable_dirs per role).

packages._comment: 'block' = never in a runtime image (H1 already removes them). 'h3_target' = development-only packages H3 removes (production-only node_modules); release-blocking until then. 'h3_target_by_role' adds role-specific ones. Names ending in /* match a whole scope.
packages._prettier: NOT a development-only package here, so it is not listed: @rab/server's email templates import @react-email/render, and both installed copies of it (1.4.0, and 1.0.4 under @react-email/components) declare prettier in dependencies and require('prettier/standalone') and 'prettier/plugins/html' at module top level; @fig/complete-commander (nest-commander, rab-ops / rab-migrate CLI) also depends on it. Verified 2026-11-03 in crewflow-h3h6/api:h3-9990a07b-amd64: loading the compiled email templates module loads 4 prettier modules from both copies (H3 #42, NEEDS-C).

provenance._comment: BuildKit provenance (mode=max) records build arguments; only these may appear, so no runner environment or credential can leak into a published attestation.
